newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London flat on Tokyo weakness.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London flat on Tokyo weakness.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were steady to lower in quiet dealing on Thursday afternoon as the market digested a sharp fall in Tokyo, traders said.

In London, the Nikkei/Ise 50 index was down 11.50 points at 1,410.98. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 Average dropped over one percent to end below the 20,500 line for the first time since early September as futures-linked selling weighed on the market.

Dealers said they were sceptical the loose alliance worked out between the Liberal Democratic Party, which earlier this month just failed to clinch a majority in parliament, and its partners would fail to reassure wary investors.

"The main worry is how spending policies will work out and it's hard to see this deal pointing the way forward. Until the political scene is clear then it's hard to see anyone wanting to take a strong view on this market," one dealer said.
A second said the Nikkei could now be set to drift down to 20,000 points amid a lack of news to inspire investors.
"The currency has come back and earnings have not been too encouraging of late...we feel the market could come back to perhaps 20,000 points," he said.
Dealers said the market was generally flat but noted some minor gains in hi-tech stocks in London.
"There seems to have been short covering there," one trader said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
